learn: Health-related fitness has five components: cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility and body composition.
Body composition is the balance of muscle, bone and fat in your body.
All five work together for good health.
check: Body composition is the balance of...
How many health-related components are there?
Do all five components work together?
lessons.try: Rate yourself 1 to 5 on each component and pick one to improve.

learn: Skill-related fitness helps in sports: agility, balance, coordination, power, reaction time and speed.
Agility is changing direction quickly. Coordination is using body parts together smoothly.
Reaction time is how fast you respond to a signal.
check: Reaction time is how fast you...
Using body parts together smoothly is...
lessons.try: Test your reaction time by catching a dropped ruler five times.

learn: Fitness tests measure your fitness, like the PACER (a shuttle run), push-ups, curl-ups and sit-and-reach.
The goal is to compare with yourself over time, not with others.
Retest every few months to see progress.
check: Fitness tests are for comparing with...
lessons.try: Do a simple fitness test at home and record your results.

learn: Dynamic warm-ups use movement: high knees, butt kicks, arm circles and walking lunges.
They raise your heart rate and body temperature.
Warm muscles are more flexible and less likely to be injured.
check: Holding a stretch for a minute
lessons.try: Lead a five-minute dynamic warm-up.

learn: Static stretching holds a position for 15 to 30 seconds.
It is best after exercise, during the cool-down.
Stretch to mild tension, never pain, and breathe normally.
lessons.try: Do a full-body static stretching routine after activity.

learn: A cool-down lowers heart rate gradually with light movement.
It helps prevent dizziness and muscle stiffness.
Hydrate during and after activity.
lessons.try: After exercise, walk for three minutes and drink water.

learn: Find your pulse at your wrist (radial) or neck (carotid) using two fingers, not your thumb.
Count beats for 15 seconds and multiply by 4 to get beats per minute.
Resting heart rate is measured when you are calm.
check: Resting heart rate is measured when you are...
lessons.try: Find your resting heart rate three mornings in a row.

learn: Moderate exercise raises your heart rate but you can still talk.
Vigorous exercise makes it hard to say more than a few words.
Kids should get vigorous activity at least three days a week.
check: Kids should get vigorous activity at least...
lessons.try: Do the "talk test" during jogging and sprinting.

learn: Recovery heart rate is how quickly your pulse returns to normal after exercise.
Fitter hearts recover faster.
Rest days and sleep help your body recover and get stronger.
check: Recovery heart rate is how fast your pulse...
lessons.try: Measure your pulse right after exercise and two minutes later.

learn: Aim with your non-throwing hand pointing at the target.
Step, rotate and follow through toward the target.
Catch with soft hands, absorbing the ball.
check: Point at the target with your...
lessons.try: Throw at a target 15 times and record hits.

learn: Use finger pads to push the ball down, keeping it at waist height.
Keep your head up to see teammates and defenders.
Protect the ball with your body and non-dribbling arm.
lessons.try: Dribble with each hand while walking a figure eight.

learn: Hold a bat, racket or hockey stick with a proper grip.
Watch the object until contact.
Swing smoothly and follow through.
lessons.try: Hit a soft ball off a tee ten times.

learn: Teams communicate with calls, signals and eye contact.
Calling "mine!" prevents collisions.
Positive talk keeps the team motivated.
lessons.try: Play a team game where you must call names before passing.

learn: Offence tries to score; defence tries to stop scoring.
Spreading out on offence creates space. Staying between the opponent and goal helps defence.
Teams plan strategies and adjust during play.
check: Between the opponent and the goal
lessons.try: Draw a simple offensive play for a team game.

learn: Everyone deserves a chance to play.
Modify games so all abilities can join, like bigger targets or softer balls.
Encourage and include classmates of all skill levels.
check: Does everyone deserve a chance to play?
lessons.try: Invent a modification so a younger sibling can play a game with you.

lessons.t: The Food Groups and Their Nutrients
learn: Fruits and vegetables give vitamins, minerals and fibre.
Grains give carbohydrates for energy. Protein foods build muscle. Dairy gives calcium and vitamin D.
A balanced diet includes all groups.
lessons.try: Plan a balanced day of meals.

learn: Breakfast refuels your body after sleep and helps concentration.
Healthy snacks combine food groups: apple slices with peanut butter, yogurt with fruit.
Avoid snacks with lots of added sugar, salt or unhealthy fats.
lessons.try: Create three healthy snack combinations.

learn: Portion size is how much food you eat at one time.
Use your hand as a guide: a fist of grains, a palm of protein.
Eat slowly and stop when you feel satisfied.
check: A fist is about a portion of...
A palm is about a portion of...
You should stop eating when you feel...
lessons.try: Use the hand guide at dinner tonight.

learn: Your body is mostly water and needs more when you're active or it's hot.
Signs of dehydration include thirst, headache, tiredness and dark urine.
Drink water throughout the day, not just when thirsty.
check: Your body needs more water when...
lessons.try: Track your water intake for one day.

learn: Soda, sweet tea and many juice drinks have large amounts of added sugar.
A can of soda can have about 10 teaspoons of sugar.
Water, milk and unsweetened drinks are better choices.
check: A can of soda has about...
Which is a better choice than soda?
lessons.try: Measure 10 teaspoons of sugar to see what's in a soda (then don't eat it!).

learn: Nutrition labels list serving size, calories and nutrients.
Check serving size first: the numbers are per serving.
Look for more fibre and protein and less added sugar and sodium.
lessons.try: Compare the labels of two snack foods.

learn: Handwashing is the best way to stop the spread of germs.
Cover coughs and sneezes, avoid sharing drinks, and keep surfaces clean.
Get enough sleep and eat well to keep your immune system strong.
check: What is the best way to stop germs spreading?
What keeps your immune system strong?
lessons.try: Make a poster about stopping germs.

learn: As you grow older, your body changes. This stage, called puberty, usually begins between ages 8 and 14.
Changes happen at different times for everyone, and that's normal.
You may need to shower more often and start using deodorant.
check: Do changes happen at the same time for everyone?
Who can you ask about growing up?
lessons.try: Talk with a parent or trusted adult about any questions you have about growing up.

learn: A daily routine includes brushing teeth, washing your face and bathing.
Change clothes and socks daily, especially after exercise.
Good routines help you feel confident and healthy.
check: How often should you change socks?
lessons.try: Write your morning and evening hygiene routines.

learn: Never share personal information online: full name, address, school, phone number or passwords.
People online may not be who they say they are.
Tell a trusted adult if anything online makes you uncomfortable.
check: Should you share your address online?
If something online makes you uncomfortable, you...
lessons.try: With a parent, review privacy settings on a device you use.

learn: For a small cut, wash with water, apply pressure and cover with a bandage.
For a nosebleed, sit up, lean forward and pinch the soft part of the nose.
For serious injuries, call 911 or get an adult right away.
check: Lean forward and pinch your nose
lessons.try: Make a simple first-aid kit list with your family.

learn: Tobacco, vaping, alcohol and drugs harm growing bodies and brains.
You can refuse by saying "No thanks," giving a reason, or walking away.
Friends who respect you won't pressure you.
check: Which is a good way to refuse?
lessons.try: Practise three ways to say no with a family member.

learn: Emotions are natural responses to situations.
Emotions can be mixed: you can feel excited and nervous at the same time.
Recognising emotions in yourself and others builds emotional intelligence.
check: Can you feel two emotions at once?
lessons.try: Keep a feelings journal for three days.

learn: Stress management strategies include exercise, deep breathing, hobbies and talking to someone.
Planning and breaking tasks into steps reduces stress about schoolwork.
Positive self-talk, like "I can do hard things", helps too.
lessons.try: Practise one stress-management strategy every day for a week.

learn: Empathy is understanding and sharing another person's feelings.
Acts of kindness, like helping or including someone, make communities stronger.
Kindness also makes the giver feel good.
check: Does kindness help the giver too?
lessons.try: Do three acts of kindness this week and write about them.
